text:
lol, I love the “he evolved” argument. 

“My paramount object in this struggle is to save the Union, and is not either to save or to destroy slavery. If I could save the Union without freeing any slave I would do it, and if I could save it by freeing all the slaves I would do it; and if I could save it by freeing some and leaving others alone I would also do that. What I do about slavery, and the colored race, I do because I believe it helps to save the Union; and what I forbear, I forbear because I do not believe it would help to save the Union." 
~ Abraham Lincoln, The Collected Works of Abraham Lincoln, Volume V, "Letter to Horace Greeley" (August 22, 1862), p. 388.

“The original proclamation has no constitutional or legal justification, except as a military measure. The exemptions were made because the military necessity did not apply to the exempted localities. Nor does that necessity apply to them now any more than it did then. If I take the step must I not do so, without the argument of military necessity…”
~ Lincoln in a letter to Salmon Chase, Sep 2, 1863

“The most that can be said of so much, is that slaves are property. Is there, has there ever been, any question that by the law of war, property, both of enemies and friends, may be taken when need? 
~ Abraham Lincoln to James Conkling (Roy P. Basler, editor, The Collected Works of Abraham Lincoln, Volume VI, p. 406-410 (Letter to James C. Conkling, August 26, 1863)

On Aug. 17, 1864, Lincoln drafted a letter to a Wisconsin newspaper editor who had previously supported the administration, but who said he could no longer do so if the president insisted on abolition. Lincoln wrote: “To me it seems plain that saying re-union and abandonment of slavery would be considered, if offered, is not saying that nothing else or less would be considered. If Jefferson Davis wishes … to know what I would do if he were to offer peace and re-union, saying nothing about slavery, let him try me.”

“My enemies say I am now carrying on this war for the sole purpose of abolition. It is and will be carried on so long as I am President for the sole purpose of restoring the Union. But no human power can subdue this rebellion without using the Emancipation lever as I have done.”
~ Abraham Lincoln, Interview with Alexander W. Randall and Joseph T. Mills (19 Aug 1864)

What year did he evolve again?

text:
Anti-Data Centers Is The New Nuclear Freeze: China Wants To End American AI Dominance, Energy Production And Everything Else https://t.co/Ou7VM2cE46 @realDonaldTrump @SpeakerJohnson @LeaderJohnThune @RepJeffries @SenSchumer 

By Robert Romano

“I would hate to see China win the war on AI... I have a sense that China is funding the opposition to AI [data] centers.”

That was  @SenRonJohnson  (R-Wis.) in a Breitbart News interview on Aug. 31 https://t.co/SdTMC5cP5I warning that the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) might be funding opposition to data centers — more than 5,400 nationwide according to Cloudscene https://t.co/QlPk1dRplV — utilized by artificial intelligence (AI) and other internet companies to store and process large amounts of data used every day on our smart phones, computers and by large critical infrastructure including financial, educational, communications, entertainment, medical, military, emergency dispatch and other government institutions, and utilities, water management and the power grid.

Just about everything we do today runs on data — and it runs on electricity, a lot of it. And to keep America’s distinct advantage globally, we need to build more of it. A lot more of it.

And China knows it. According to an estimate by cyber security firm Alethea, China, Russia and other foreign adversaries have been actively promoting anti-data center propaganda on state media, with social media bots providing echo chambers: “The most attributable layer is overt state media, which is already running at full steam. The message pushed by Russia, China, and Iran largely converges around the idea that America is hoarding power and water for the elites while ordinary people suffer, with each country tailoring messaging to their respective geopolitical interests and domestic audiences…” https://t.co/rbeJKK2mog

There are several propaganda pieces promoting increasing electricity prices, China’s AI buildout succeeding while the U.S. fails and local opposition to data centers: “What domestic actors seed and foreign-linked networks amplify, the AI slop machine scales, producing a volume of emotionally resonant, locally targeted content that is difficult to attribute, harder to counter, and arrives faster than comms teams can respond.”

If this all sounds familiar, it should.

It's the modern-day nuclear freeze movement. In the Cold War, State Department analyses show the Soviets actively funded fronts like the World Peace Council to stoke fears of the dangers of nuclear war and to push for unilateral disarmament. https://t.co/tyEd3gbE5g

Well, it was a bad idea then, and it’s a bad idea now. The KGB did not invent American fear of the bomb, but it did exploit it. The same thing is happening today.

The need to build out technology, energy and mineral infrastructure including rare earths lies at the heart of President Donald Trump’s plan to protect our economic and national security. And today's opposition is just as dangerous as it was in the 1980s.

In May, Treasury @SecScottBessent, speaking at 2026 Reagan Economic Forum in Simi Valley, Calif. warned of the danger: “Somewhere along the way, we lost sight of a foundational principle that previous generations understood instinctively: economic security is national security, for a nation that cannot manufacture, mine, ship, or refine its needs gradually cedes its strength—and sovereignty—to others. That is a dangerous dependency for any country. It is an unacceptable one for the United States.” https://t.co/01VRpwgYoB

Bessent added, “[S]ecure supply chains matter as much as stock indices. That productive capacity is power. That trade policy, industrial policy, and national security policy must all fit together, or they will each fail separately.” He’s right.

If we get into a world war with China or Russia we might lack the manufacturing capacity to keep up with producing planes, tanks, bombs, ships, missiles, drones, etc. because of decades of outsourcing that is still being reversed.

In 10 or 15 years, such a conflict might be AI-driven, with automated weapons systems, and the country with the most compute and the most electricity — and who could keep those systems running amid a vast assault — would be the power that wins. It is not hard to imagine a contest pitting one nation’s artificial general intelligence versus another’s.

China is already pre-positioning inside U.S. energy, water, and communications networks to conduct more cyberattacks, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency reports. https://t.co/MCvhucP6qe In an actual shooting war, it will be much worse.

To compete — and to deter threats — to borrow a phrase from Captain Kirk: We need more power.

At a Potterville, Mich. Rally in August 2024, President Donald Trump warned that the U.S. needs to double electricity output to compete with China on AI, stating “For us to compete successfully with China and others on AI, we’re going to need twice the electricity that we currently produce. Can you believe that? We’re not going to be even close. The only guy that can do that is a guy like me.” https://t.co/wqLH52m9RM

But electricity output increased by 2.8 percent in 2025, from 4.308 trillion kilowatthours in 2024 to 4.429 trillion kilowatthours (kWh), according to the latest data compiled by the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA). https://t.co/ViDZdBu2SD At that pace, it will take more than two decades to double the grid.

Tech companies including xAI, Meta, Amazon, Oracle and others are already increasing electricity generation on site, https://t.co/eZh8NPrAon but the bigger projects could still be a few years off — and we’re still nowhere close to the President’s goal. We’ve got a long way to go.

Besides how long it takes to get new power stations online, one reason for the slow growth of America’s grid is because of lawsuits against America’s electric and other energy producers. On June 25, 2025, @SenTedCruz  (R-Texas) chaired a hearing https://t.co/hpHyVfbhmO at the Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Federal Courts, Oversight, Agency Action, and Federal Rights entitled, “Enter the Dragon—China and the Left’s Lawfare Against American Energy Dominance.”

At the hearing, Cruz laid out the scheme, alleging, “There is a coordinated assault by the radical left, backed and paid for by the Chinese Communist Party to seize control of our courts, to weaponize litigation against U.S. energy producers. All in order to undermine American energy dominance. At stake, is a lot more than an industry. Our energy sector is the engine of American prosperity, the lifeblood of our industrial power, our national security, and our geopolitical leverage…. [F]oreign money from entities tied to the Chinese Communist Party flows into the United States to bankroll climate advocacy groups who litigate against American Energy… [A]ctivist lawyers flood our courts with lawsuits designed not to win policy debates but to bankrupt energy producers and to dismantle energy infrastructure through sheer attrition.” https://t.co/eBuWpUB2Tx

This is not the first time Beijing has meddled in the U.S. legal system. A Nov. 2023 Bloomberg News report by Emily Siegel, “China Firm Funds U.S. Suits Amid Push to Disclose Foreign Ties” found China-backed firms funding litigation in U.S. patent courts. https://t.co/uUlrfBqS4h

To address the threat of foreign influence in American courts undermining economic and national security, Congressional Republicans have offered vital legislation. The Protecting Our Courts from Foreign Manipulation Act,  H.R. 2675, https://t.co/eRp3Qsrd5d by U.S. @RepBenCline  (R-Va.), would prohibit or require disclosure of certain foreign-backed litigation funding arrangements. And the Litigation Transparency Act, H.R. 1109, https://t.co/RSqwpqNd4X by U.S. @repdarrellissa  (R-Calif.) would require parties in federal civil cases to disclose when outside financiers have a financial stake in litigation.

In addition, President Trump could issue executive orders under the Corporate Transparency Act for the Treasury Department to designate litigation funders as entities required to report their beneficial owners and under the Bank Secrecy Act to trigger additional reporting requirements.

To reach President Trump’s goal of doubling electricity output and remaining number one in technology including AI, we need all-of-the-above — whatever it takes, get more coal, nuclear, solar and everything else that has capacity to grow. In the meantime, China is able to exponentially expand, uses subsidies freely and without the federal, state and local barriers we artificially put in our own way — while Congress has appeared reluctant to subsidize at the levels that might be necessary to compete long term. America’s industrial policy along with its grid needs a substantial upgrade.

Hopefully, it will not take an emergency like Pearl Harbor to again awaken a sleeping giant. Peace through strength means that to secure peace, we must prepare for war. In so doing, we deter the next Pearl Harbor, the next 9/11.
